science.title: The Planet That Lied About Its Own Spin
science.description: A new study warns that astronomers measuring the rotation of distant exoplanets may often be measuring atmospheric winds instead, since the clouds of Venus circle the planet roughly 60 times faster than Venus itself actually spins. Kane proposes using multi-wavelength observations to correct for this, work that will matter enormously once the European Space Agency's PLATO mission launches in 2027 and, researchers predict, discovers several hundred Venus like exoplanets.

science.title: Synergistic effect and comparative study of CoMn2O4 and MnCo2O4 spinel nanoparticles as promising materials for electrochemical hydrogen storage
science.description: The development of stable electrode materials with high performance, based on transition metals, is vital for advancing energy storage applications. This study reports the synthesis of CoMn2O4 and MnCo2O4 spinel nanoparticles (SNPs) via a wet-chemistry method, and investigates their performance as electrode materials for electrochemical hydrogen storage. XRD analysis confirmed the formation of highly crystalline spinel structures for both samples, with an average crystallite size of 32 nm. FE-SEM imaging revealed that the CoMn2O4 and MnCo2O4 SNPs exhibit an agglomerated, polyhedral morphology, with mean particle sizes of 49 and 53 nm, respectively. BET analysis confirmed the mesoporous structure of the samples. Electrochemical studies, including cyclic voltammetry and chronopotentiometry, demonstrated excellent electrochemical performance. CoMn2O4 and MnCo2O4 SNPs exhibited a specific capacitance (Csp) of 417 and 424 F/g, at a scan rate of 10 mV/s. Furthermore, CoMn2O4 and MnCo2O4 SNPs showcased hydrogen storage capacities of 1930 and 1594 mAh/g, respectively, following 10 charge–discharge cycles. These results highlight the potential of the samples as promising candidates for electrochemical hydrogen storage.

science.title: Generation of negative acoustic radiation forces
science.description: Negative acoustic radiation forces act opposite to the direction of wave propagation. While this force reversal has been demonstrated for sub-wavelength particles, achieving it on objects larger than the acoustic wavelength (λ) remains challenging and has typically been demonstrated in limited cases. Expanding on the concept of acoustic pulling, we present a method to generate negative radiation forces on elastic spheres comparable to or larger than λ using a focused multi-element array. Unlike previous demonstrations requiring sources that surround the object or the object to have specific material properties or geometries, we generate tailored acoustic beams that impart negative forces on solid glass spheres positioned 9.5 centimeters away from the transducer’s aperture plane. The beams exhibit an on-axis null region and refocus the pressure behind the sphere, thus minimizing backscatter and enabling the force direction reversal. Experiments and simulations confirm negative radiation forces on spheres with diameters up to 3λ. These results provide a promising framework for developing acoustic tractor beams for non-contact manipulation in environments such as biological benchtop settings, microgravity, and manufacturing.

science.title: Depletion of davemaoite in Earth’s ambient lower mantle
science.description: The mineralogy of the Earth’s lower mantle is fundamental to understanding the planet’s formation, composition, evolution, and dynamics. However, uncertainties in the elastic properties and phase transitions of CaSiO₃ davemaoite—the third most abundant phase in a pyrolitic lower mantle—have hindered quantitative links between seismic observations and lower-mantle mineralogy. Here we combine Brillouin spectroscopy with resistively heated diamond anvil cell experiments to measure the sound velocities of CaSiO₃ davemaoite up to 80 GPa and 973 K. We show that the tetragonal–cubic phase transition occurs below 900 K throughout the entire lower mantle. Fitting the thermoelastic properties of cubic davemaoite reveals substantially reduced shear-wave velocities at deep lower-mantle conditions. Because of these intrinsically slow velocities, increasing bridgmanite abundance alone cannot reconcile seismic observations for a normal lower mantle containing even small amount of davemaoite. Our results therefore suggest that davemaoite is depleted in the ambient lower mantle but concentrated within LLSVPs, likely as a consequence of late-stage crystallization during magma-ocean differentiation. Davemaoite remains cubic throughout most of the lower mantle and exhibits intrinsically low shear-wave velocities. Seismic constraints indicate that it is depleted in the ambient lower mantle but enriched within LLSVPs, likely as a result of late-stage crystallization during magma-ocean differentiation.

science.title: Ryugu and Bennu preserve primordial isotopic heterogeneity absent from the meteorite record
science.description: Ivuna-type (CI) carbonaceous chondrites are commonly used as proxies for the composition of the planet-forming disk because their chemical abundances resemble those of the solar photosphere. However, their isotopic uniformity may reflect pervasive alteration and isotopic averaging rather than preservation of the earliest Solar System reservoirs. Here we show that samples returned from the asteroids Ryugu and Bennu preserve isotopic heterogeneity in major planet-building elements, including magnesium, silicon, and iron, that is absent from CI chondrites and unresolved in other meteorites. These signatures reveal isotopically distinct components that are absent from, or homogenized in, known CI chondrites. We infer that Bennu and Ryugu retain a record of primordial isotopic diversity that was not completely homogenized during disk and parent-body processing. Thus, returned asteroid samples provide access to previously unsampled Solar System material that preserves early isotopic components not fully represented in the meteorite record. Samples returned from Ryugu and Bennu preserve primordial isotopic heterogeneity in major planet-building elements that is not represented in meteorite collections.
